name: Impeccable
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and more
short: Makes your coding agent better at design, so sites stop looking AI-made.
what: A design skill with 24 commands, plus a checker with 61 rules, that steers your coding agent away from the generic look of AI-made websites (Inter everywhere, purple gradients, cards inside cards).
who: Anyone building websites or app screens with an AI coding agent: developers, indie hackers and designers who code.
needs: A coding agent. The README lists Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Pi and others
Node.js for the installer. The npm package asks for Node 22.18 or later
No API key. The checker runs without an AI model

steps.title: Install from your project folder
steps.text: It detects which agents you use and asks whether to install for this project or everywhere. Reload your agent afterwards.

steps.title: Or, in Claude Code, use the plugin
steps.text: Then open /plugin and install Impeccable from the list.

steps.title: Or, in VS Code with Copilot

try.label: From the README
try.text:
/impeccable init

Then try:
/impeccable critique landing
/impeccable audit the header

(In Codex, type $impeccable instead. To check a folder without an agent: npx impeccable detect src/)

watch: The installer adds a design hook that runs the checker every time your agent edits a UI file. In Claude Code, hooks run even if you deny the command, so the first edit can download its engine. Install with `--no-hooks` if you don't want that.
In Codex you have to approve the hook in /hooks after installing or updating.
It saves working files to a `.impeccable/` folder. The README gives a `.gitignore` block so screenshots don't get committed.
